plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers directly from the ground in autumn, without any leaves present. The leaves emerge the following spring and die back by summer. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (September to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling. Its leafless blooming earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial forming dense clumps topped with plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects preparing for winter or migration.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: Native to North America in meadows, roadsides, and prairies; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time but has airborne pollen; goldenrod pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum x morifolium
plants.description: A widely cultivated perennial with daisy-like to pompon-shaped flower heads in many forms. Its blooming is triggered by shortening day length, making it a classic autumn flower in gardens and florists' shops.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn to early winter (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Originated in East Asia (China and Japan); cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and the flower is the emblem of the Japanese Imperial family and the subject of Japan's annual Chrysanthemum Festival.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub with feathery-looking foliage that covers itself in fragrant, fluffy golden flower balls in late winter and spring, as the Southern Hemisphere warms up.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
